question: An investigator is developing a drug that results in contraction of the pupillary dilator muscle when instilled topically. The drug works by increasing neurotransmitter release from the presynaptic nerve terminal. When administered intravenously, this drug is most likely to have which of the following additional effects?

options.opc: Relaxation of the bladder neck sphincter
options.opd: Release of epinephrine by the adrenal medulla

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Drug increases neurotransmitter release from presynaptic nerve terminal -> activates sympathetic nervous system -> release of epinephrine by the adrenal medulla -> 80% CHAIN: Drug increases neurotransmitter release from presynaptic nerve terminal -> activates sympathetic nervous system -> contraction of skeletal muscles -> 70% CHAIN: Drug increases neurotransmitter release from presynaptic nerve terminal -> activates parasympathetic nervous system -> acceleration of gut peristalsis -> 60% CHAIN: Drug increases neurotransmitter release from presynaptic nerve terminal -> activates parasympathetic nervous system -> relaxation of the bladder neck sphincter -> 50% CHAIN: Drug increases neurotransmitter release from presynaptic nerve terminal -> affects autonomic nervous system -> increase in pyloric sphincter tone -> 80%
enhanced_information: The drug, by increasing neurotransmitter release from the presynaptic nerve terminal, is likely to activate the sympathetic nervous system, leading to the release of epinephrine by the adrenal medulla. This aligns with consensus. The option most likely to occur when the drug is administered intravenously is the release of epinephrine by the adrenal medulla (opd).
analysis: The drug, by increasing neurotransmitter release from the presynaptic nerve terminal, activates the sympathetic nervous system, leading to the release of epinephrine by the adrenal medulla. This aligns with consensus and is the most likely effect when the drug is administered intravenously.
